<observation>
  <type>bugfix</type>
  <title>Fixed UserCache.get null placeholder race with computeIfAbsent</title>
  <subtitle>Replaced plain cache.get(id) with atomic computeIfAbsent so concurrent callers cannot both write a null placeholder.</subtitle>
  <facts>
    <fact>UserCache.get changed from `cache.get(id)` to `cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load)` in src/main/java/com/acme/cache/UserCache.java.</fact>
    <fact>The previous `cache.get(id)` allowed two concurrent callers to both observe a missing entry and both write a null placeholder.</fact>
    <fact>`computeIfAbsent` makes the load atomic: the first caller invokes `loader::load` while other callers wait for the same mapping.</fact>
    <fact>CacheConcurrencyTest passes after the change, confirming the concurrent null-placeholder race is resolved.</fact>
  </facts>
  <narrative>UserCache.get previously performed a plain `cache.get(id)` read, which left a race window: two concurrent callers could both find the entry absent, both invoke the loader, and both write a null placeholder (or duplicate value). The fix replaces the read with `cache.computeIfAbsent(id, loader::load)`, delegating the conditional load to the map's atomic compute-if-absent primitive. This guarantees only one caller performs `loader::load` for a given id and that the others observe the same mapping. The accompanying CacheConcurrencyTest now passes, pinning the previously failing concurrent scenario.</narrative>
